data.title: SBA Advances Saudi TV Sector, Nurtures National Talent on World Television Day
data.content:
Jeddah, November 21, 2026, SPA -- As the world marks World Television Day on November 21, Saudi Arabia’s television sector, led by the Saudi Broadcasting Authority (SBA), continues to advance as a key contributor to national development, delivering reliable media, nurturing national talent, and keeping pace with the Kingdom’s transformation under Saudi Vision 2030.
    The occasion, established by the United Nations in 1996, recognizes television’s profound influence on audiences and its role in disseminating knowledge, raising awareness, and promoting dialogue and cultural exchange among nations. With its broad reach and ability to connect audiences, television serves as a window to the world, delivering content that contributes to the progress of societies. It also plays a key role in sharing news and information and educating diverse segments of society on scientific and intellectual issues.
    In this context, SBA has pursued initiatives to advance the sector and reinforce its role in national development. Throughout its evolution, the authority has continued to serve the public while focusing on nurturing talent, supporting national professionals, and empowering and recognizing skilled individuals.
    SBA has also kept pace with rapid technological advances worldwide, seeking to meet the aspirations of the public through high-quality, responsible, modern media that caters to varied interests. Its efforts align with the Kingdom’s growth across sectors and the broader digital transformation agenda, including the use of technology to improve quality and make valuable archival material more accessible to wider audiences.
    With the support of Minister of Media Salman Al-Dossary, the authority has continued to strengthen its role in enriching television content through new programming cycles, digital transformation, and initiatives to develop the local media market. These efforts aim to deliver content that reflects the Kingdom’s standing and keeps pace with its ongoing transformation.
    SBA CEO Ali Al-Zaid underscored the authority’s commitment to investing in its human capital in response to the changing media landscape. He said its strategy focuses on advancing the sector while meeting audience preferences, empowering the local television market, fostering a competitive and engaging environment, and increasing domestic media production.
    This approach is reflected in a diverse range of programming, including news, drama, entertainment, religious programs, family-oriented shows, and folklore, distributed through traditional and digital platforms.
    Al-Zaid also highlighted the authority’s commitment to meeting audience expectations and enriching society’s cultural identity through diverse content produced and broadcast in line with international standards.
    He noted that Saudi television has restructured its internal operations around new programming cycles that place audiences at the center and strengthen connections with viewers through locally produced content that meets international standards. The aim is to present the Saudi story to the world authentically and accurately by documenting the Kingdom’s development and achievements.
    -- SPA
